maya: Heads up — small but consistent BLEU drop (~2.1 BLEU) on cn-jp mixed test after int8 quantization of astra-v2-lite when prefix/KV cache is enabled. Repro steps and samples below.

maya: sacrebleu baseline (fp16): 32.8
maya: sacrebleu int8 + prefix_cache=true: 30.7
maya: noticed katakana tokens merging with trailing punctuation in detok: "コンマ," ends up being split/merged differently -> alignment shifts.

maya: repro curl to reproduce quickly:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/dev/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"astra-v2-lite:int8","prompt":"今日は、コンマ、テストです。","prefix_cache":true}'
```

raj: can you paste a minimal src/ref pair where detok differs?

maya: short sample:
src: "今日は、コンマ、テストです。"
ref: "今天，测试。"
int8 out (prefix cache on): "今日は、コンマ, テストです。"  <-- ASCII comma token appears next to katakana and shifts tokenization

li-wei: that smells like a tokenizer path divergence when using optimized int8 kernels. we saw q4 variants change byte-split behavior earlier. try running with explicit unicode normalization (NFKC) or with `tokenize(raw=false)` to see if it changes.

ana: (typo fix) — ran sacrebleu with detok=13, case=True — numbers match Maya's drop. also ran chrF++ and COMET quick checks: chrF down ~0.9, COMET delta -0.05. consistent but not huge.

sam: can you try same int8 build with `prefix_cache=false`? if KV caching stashes raw bytes vs normalized tokens that could cause boundary shifts on refill.

maya: ran that — int8 + prefix_cache=false sacrebleu 32.5 (basically back to fp16). so strongly correlated with prefix cache.

raj: nice signal. next steps: bisect commits between kernel-selector changes and the prefix-cache refactor. @ci-bot can you kick an eval matrix for astra-v2-lite with combinations: fp16/int8 x prefix_cache true/false x token_norm on/off?

ci-bot: started job #ci/ast-av2-quant-eval-3123456789
ci-bot: matrix queued: [fp16,prefix=false], [fp16,prefix=true], [int8,prefix=false], [int8,prefix=true]

li-wei: i'll also add a unit test that detoks and asserts punctuation boundaries for katakana/han mixed inputs (small fixture). pushing in a sec.

ana: note — this only reproduces on mixed JP/ZH inputs where punctuation is U+FF0C (fullwidth comma) vs ASCII comma. looks like NFKC/NFKD differences plus the optimized tokenizer path.

sam: quick mitigation idea: re-run normalization on the prefix chunk during KV cache refill before merging. cheap to add but need to measure perf regression under high QPS.

maya: filing a regression ticket with attached samples + eval logs. links: 
- gist with raw samples: https://gist.github.com/redwood/abc123
- CI job: https://ci.redwood/ast-av2-quant-eval-3123456789

maya: thanks everyone :thumbsup:

raj: great catch. once CI finishes we'll decide if this becomes a hotfix or waits for the next rollout. :eyes:
